nodes.name: New Email Form Submission
nodes.notes: Serves an n8n-hosted form (From, Subject, Receivedat). Each submission becomes one execution.

nodes.name: Download from Google Drive
nodes.notes: Downloads the file's binary content from Google Drive so the next node can parse it. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2. Google Cloud Console → enable Drive API → OAuth2 client or Service Account.

nodes.name: Parse CSV Contents
nodes.notes: Parses the incoming CSV binary into JSON items.

nodes.name: Clean & Reshape Rows
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Normalize incoming email records to a stable schema Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Rows Pass Validation?
nodes.notes: Two-way gate on ={{ $json.messageId }}. TRUE continues the happy path, FALSE takes the alternate branch. Watch out: The false branch carries the non-matching items — wire it deliberately rather than leaving it dangling.

nodes.name: Quarantine Bad Rows
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Email Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Load Rows into Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Upserts a row into 'Email Tracker', matched on messageId — re-running with the same key updates the row instead of duplicating it. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Repack as XLSX
nodes.notes: Serializes items to a XLSX binary file.

nodes.name: Archive Processed File (Google Drive)
nodes.notes: Uploads the generated file to Google Drive as a timestamped archive copy. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2. Google Cloud Console → enable Drive API → OAuth2 client or Service Account.

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per email (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.name: Serialize Run Output (CSV)
nodes.notes: Serializes items to a CSV binary file.

nodes.name: Archive Copy to Google Drive
nodes.notes: Uploads the generated file to Google Drive as a timestamped archive copy. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2. Google Cloud Console → enable Drive API → OAuth2 client or Service Account.

nodes.name: Summarize Run Stats
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes runAt, itemCount, status. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Email Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

# Save applications: Google Sheets

**Pattern:** Form Intake · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Form

## Overview

Starts when the form is submitted, and covers drip-campaigns work end to end across Google Sheets, Google Drive and Slack.

It moves through 16 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. New Email Form Submission
2. Download from Google Drive
3. Parse CSV Contents
4. Clean & Reshape Rows
5. Rows Pass Validation?
6. Quarantine Bad Rows
7. Load Rows into Google Sheets
8. Repack as XLSX
9. Archive Processed File (Google Drive)
10. Fingerprint for Idempotency
11. Drop Already-Processed Items
12. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
13. Archive Copy to Google Drive
14. Summarize Run Stats
15. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
16. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing drip-campaigns work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

New Email Form Submission → Download from Google Drive → Parse CSV Contents → Clean & Reshape Rows → Rows Pass Validation? → Quarantine Bad Rows → Load Rows into Google Sheets → Repack as XLSX → Archive Processed File (Google Drive) → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Copy to Google Drive → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Google Drive aligned by hand for drip campaigns
- Intake checked for completeness before it is stored in Google Sheets, for drip campaigns
- Drip campaigns work where "Download from Google Drive" is still a manual step before Google Sheets
- Drip campaigns work that only reaches Google Sheets when a form is submitted, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Google Drive in step for drip campaigns, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Google Sheets or Google Drive are skipped, across all 19 nodes of this drip-campaigns build
- A failed Google Sheets or Google Drive call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 19 nodes in this drip-campaigns build
- Fans the same result out to Slack in the same run, for drip campaigns
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 19 nodes for drip campaigns before wiring Google Sheets

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2; Google OAuth2 / service account; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Bad rows are quarantined into their own store, not dropped silently and not allowed to break the whole batch — one malformed row in a 10,000-row file shouldn't stop the other 9,999 from loading, but it also shouldn't vanish without a trace.

## Practice exercises

Already production-grade — deepen your understanding:

1. Feed it a file with a few deliberately malformed rows and confirm they land in quarantine, not the main store.
2. Switch the source format (e.g. csv to xlsx) and see how little actually has to change.
3. Turn on archive mode and confirm the processed file gets repacked and stored.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Drive API → OAuth2 client or Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Service Accounts have their own empty Drive — share the target folder with it.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your drip campaigns process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Google Drive: scope the credential to the one folder this workflow writes to, not `drive.readonly` across the account.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.

**Do not log**
drip-campaigns payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
